correctness.rationale: A positive equilibrium forces b_i>0 or an incoming link at each node. For any c>0 either rational activating or inhibiting link satisfies h(cs)/h(s) between min(c,c^-1) and max(c,c^-1); this gives forward invariance of the history-dependent positive box. In logarithmic coordinates, integrate the partial derivatives of (-d_i x_i+b_i+sum h_ij)/x_i along the geometric interpolation to the equilibrium. The exact diagonal coefficient is ∫(b_i+sum h_ij(z_j))/z_i ds, while off-diagonal coefficients are ∫z_j h_ij'(z_j)/z_i ds. The identity s|h'(s)|=h(s)-h(s)^2/a implies A_i−sum|C_ij|≥δ_r>0 and sum|C_ij|≤B_r on the invariant box. A weighted sup norm, first-crossing comparison with delayed terms and η+B_r(exp(ητ)−1)<δ_r give |log(x_i(t)/bar x_i)|≤r exp(−ηt) for t≥0. This also proves uniqueness of the strictly positive equilibrium. Independent rational checks of both derivative signs and example rates passed; finite samples are not the proof.
residual_risks: Finite checks are not universal proofs.
Convergence is conditional on existence of positive equilibrium, not an existence classification.
